# LovelyCarve FileVault integration

Upstream: https://github.com/SecurityRonin/filevault-forensic , commit
857e04033e09c84324948b2cbfdd9e043b24d62b, core + forensic 0.1.5, Apache-2.0.
License and source comments are retained. The vendored workspace uses Rust 1.99,
matching the host; the optional upstream VFS adapter is not enabled by the app.

Local additions: storage.rs / storage_metadata.rs / storage_plist.rs authenticate
neither attackers nor disks; they validate format CRC, bounds, version, copies,
transaction/OID association and CF reference expansion. Multiple LV inventory,
validated multi-segment reads, recovery protectors, VMK/XTS pair and optional
external XML/wipekey contexts are provided through storage::Container.
FileVaultVolume / parse_info convenience functions use this validated path and
reject ambiguous multi-LV selection. Legacy public context/metadata extractors
are retained for low-level compatibility and are not the production entry point.
The plaintext reader now errors on truncated ciphertext; keys have redacted Debug
and zeroization. Password KDF attempts are bounded and cancellation is checked.

The app uses core and forensic::audit_info, with a typed inspection command and
the existing encrypted-volume unlock workflow. No libfvde source was copied;
it was used for format/API comparison. All 88 APIs and unsupported layouts are
recorded in [FILEVAULT.md](../../docs/formats/FILEVAULT.md).

Validation: just test-filevault; just clippy-filevault. FVDE_ORACLE_IMAGE points
at the raw dfvfs fvdetest CoreStorage partition; the public qcow/raw source is
kept outside this repository. Synthetics are generated by core::test_support,
while independent sector digests remain in core/tests/oracle_fvde.rs.
